title: Rendered audio lands ~42-52 ms after the video timeline, so captions lead the heard word slightly
summary: Measured on a SpiderVideo render: a voice starting at 0.500 s in its source file starts at 0.542 s in the output (second phrase 5.002 -> 5.054 s), with stream start_time 0 on both tracks. The cause is not established (consistent with audio-encoder priming) and it affects music too. Ducking is applied inside the render and stays aligned with the voice as heard; captions follow the video timeline, so they appear ~1-1.5 frames before the heard word. Rarely visible — do not shift every caption token unless you measured your own output against its source. Measured more precisely in SPI3-70 (2026-09-28): a whole-file cross-correlation of the voice stem against a render gives exactly 2048 samples at 48 kHz (42.67 ms) — two AAC frames, i.e. encoder priming the file does not compensate for.
references: SpiderIQ PR #4188 (SC-465, merged 2026-09-22) — measured during the audio-lane build; recorded in docs/services/SpiderVideo/LEARNINGS.md 'Remotion's encoded audio lands ~42-52 ms after the composition timeline'
